title: Decision: write-before-ioctl pattern for KEY_IMPORT
description: KEY_IMPORT uses a two-phase pattern: write() accumulates raw key bytes in inbuf, then the ioctl carries only metadata. This is correct for three independent reasons: (1) asymmetric keys exceed the inline key cap (128 bytes) — RSA/ML-DSA keys are 256B-4896B; (2) the ioctl struct's fixed size works identically on 32/64-bit userspace with no compat_ioctl; (3) inbuf_clear() memzero_explicit zeroizes key bytes on every path after KEY_IMPORT. A reviewer suggesting 'embed key bytes directly in the ioctl struct like the inline INIT key' ignores that this would require 8KB stack allocations per ioctl call and a full 32/64-bit compat layer.
close_reason: Reviewed, documented, and hardened in CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, and AGENTS.md
